tasks.short: Review paperwork so counting errors do not become shortages

steps.what: Sign which paperwork checks may run
Monitor paperwork systems for error-related shortages
Flag gaps with the signed paperwork rule
Classify the note on a flagged document

loop.input: free-text reason and the signed reason codes
loop.check: The label is one of the signed reason codes
loop.stop: One pass; unmatched notes wait and no person is named as the cause
loop.why_not_simpler: A free-text reason is not a fixed code

steps.what: Correct the paperwork the rule flagged

tasks.design: The loss prevention manager signs which paperwork checks run: receiving, transfer and stock count, matched on store, document id and quantity in the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. A fixed rule flags a missing document or a quantity mismatch. A bounded pass labels a free-text reason against the signed codes, and the manager decides which procedure to change. The check does not name an employee.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shortage reviews started from paper files and a spreadsheet, so a missing transfer could not be tied to one document id.
tasks.enabler_now: Receiving, transfer and count documents can share a store id, a document id and two quantities.
tasks.still_hard: A mismatch with no quantities, and the choice to change a procedure, still need the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides which gaps are errors in the paperwork and which procedure should change.

ambition.what: Review paperwork gaps every week from the signed checks, not only after a shortage is found

tasks.altitude: Complete documents that match drop off the list. The manager's week is the unmatched paper and the procedure choice. Nobody is scored.

reach.task: Correct the document the signed check flagged
reach.learn: Which document ids failed and which procedure the manager changed

evidence.claim: Digest [S1] describes a versioned policy library where a model classifies and summarises rules and flags gaps, which fits a check of paperwork procedures rather than a verdict on a person.
In a mid-size retailer, error-related shortages show up as missing receiving, transfer or count documents, and the hard part is the paper that has no quantities.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, so a paperwork gap is not an action about an employee.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends when a signed procedure note is filed or a document is sent back for correction. Speaking to a named employee about a shortage is outside this task.

Input contract: document type (receiving, transfer, count), store id, document id, expected quantity, recorded quantity, status, free-text reason. Producer is the stock paperwork export. A row with no document id, or with either quantity missing, is not flagged and stays on a manual list. No employee id.
Native document status in the stock record is configured before custom code. The meeting prior does not fit: time today is on documents and screens.
unknowns: Which document type is the system of record for transfers.
How often quantities are blank rather than wrong.
Who may sign the weekly checks when the manager is absent.
research_questions: What share of shortage reviews start from a document with a blank quantity?
How often does a flagged mismatch turn out to be a late posting?

already_counted.description: Manager time on unmatched reasons stays in the classification review
Manager time choosing a procedure change stays in that decision

incremental.description: Revise reason codes when a new document type starts causing shortages
Stores resubmit a document the check sent back

approvals.approved_version: paperwork checks signed for this week
procedure note signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many documents lack quantities, so the flag rarely runs and the manager still reads the paper. The high case assumes complete quantities but every procedure change is still signed by the manager. Conversations with a named employee are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise stores on how to write loss-investigation procedures

loop.input: gap note and versioned procedure sections
loop.output: draft section that cites a section id
loop.check: Every requirement cites a section id and the text leaves interviews and named decisions with a person
loop.stop: One draft; if no section id matches, leave the section blank and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Advice on a local gap is not a fixed clause

steps.what: Advise the store on investigation procedures
Confirm the store can follow it

tasks.design: A versioned procedure in {DOCS} is the only source a draft may cite. The store manager describes a local gap, a bounded draft proposes a section that keeps interviews and any decision about a named employee with a person, and the loss prevention manager signs the text. Stores see only the signed version. The draft does not run an investigation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local investigation habits lived in mail and memory, so a draft could not show which signed procedure section it was changing.
tasks.enabler_now: The procedure can be stored as versioned sections with an id, which a draft can cite or leave blank.
tasks.still_hard: What a store should actually do when something is missing, and whether the text is fit to publish, is still the manager's advice.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides the procedure text and keeps every investigation with a person.

ambition.what: Smaller stores receive a signed investigation procedure without waiting for a site visit

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time retyping the same section and keeps the right to refuse a draft. Advising the store stays a conversation. Investigations do not move.

reach.task: Follow the signed investigation procedure instead of a local habit
reach.learn: Which section is current and which local gap the manager rejected

evidence.claim: Digest [S1] describes a versioned policy library where a model classifies and summarises rules and flags gaps, so a procedure draft can cite a section and a person still decides.
Digest [S15] says a model-drafted paid report cited sources that did not exist, so a person stays on a procedure before it is published.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, so the procedure must keep that decision with a person.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends when a signed procedure is published. Running an investigation or an interview is out of scope and stays person_does elsewhere.

Input contract: policy id, version, section id, store id, local gap note. Producer of the gap note is the store manager. Producer of the policy is the document store. If no section id matches the gap, the draft leaves that section blank and stops.
Native document versions and read receipts are configured before custom code. The published text must say a person runs interviews and decides any action about a named employee.
unknowns: Whether each store may keep a local annex or must use one company text.
Who may sign a procedure when the manager is absent.
Whether the works council must see a procedure that tells staff how incidents are handled.
research_questions: How many stores still use a procedure with no version id?
How often does the manager reject a drafted section?

already_counted.description: Manager edits a section that cites the wrong policy id
Advice conversation stays with the manager

incremental.description: Update the section list when the company procedure version changes
Stores resubmit a gap note that named no section

approvals.approved_version: investigation procedure signed in this advice

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes local practice is still oral, so the draft has nothing to cite and the manager still writes the section. The high case assumes a versioned procedure but every published text is still signed in a conversation with the store. Investigation meetings are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep bad-check logs, offender reports and alarm lists

steps.what: Sign the register rules for this period
Enter bad-check rows in the databases
Maintain alarm activation lists from signed rules
Add a name on the multiple offenders report
Review multiple offenders reports for duplicates

tasks.design: The loss prevention manager signs the register rules in {DOCS}: a bad-check or alarm row needs store, date and amount or device, and the alarm activation list has no name. A {WORKFLOW} job applies those rules. A name is added to the multiple-offenders report only when the manager types it. No rule matches people or scores staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bad checks, repeat cases and alarm activations were rekeyed into spreadsheets, so a row could not be rejected for a missing store or date.
tasks.enabler_now: An event can carry store, date, amount and device id, which is enough to file an alarm list and to hold a name back.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding that a person belongs on the offender report is a decision about a person, and duplicate names the rule cannot see still need a reader.
tasks.human_edge: The manager is the only one who may add a name, and can refuse to add one.

ambition.what: Decide the same week whether a name may be added, instead of leaving the request in mail

tasks.altitude: Alarm rows without a name file themselves under the signed rules. The manager's remaining work is the name decision and the duplicates a rule cannot see.

reach.task: Read who signed the register rules and which names were added by a person
reach.learn: Which rules are current and which name requests are still unsigned

evidence.claim: Digest [S8] says a new incident register increased reports sharply, and that is more reporting, not fewer incidents, so a longer alarm list is not more crime.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, so a name is added only by the manager.
Digest [S3] says incident reports are forwarded to the person in charge, so a name request waits for the manager and is not sent onward by the register.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task maintains three registers. It does not match identities, score people, or decide that someone is an offender.

Input contract: event type (bad check, alarm activation, name request), store id, date, amount or device id, check reference, name or blank. Producer of the event is the store manager. A row with no store or no date is rejected. The alarm list is store and device only. A name is stored only on the offenders report and only from the manager's signed entry.

Native register forms are configured before custom code. The meeting prior does not fit: time today is on the screen and a spreadsheet. Works council consent applies if the register is later used to monitor staff, which this design does not do.
unknowns: Whether bad checks are still taken in these stores.
Who may see the offenders report.
How long a name entry is kept.
research_questions: What share of alarm rows arrive with no device id?
How many name requests does the manager refuse in a typical month?

already_counted.description: Manager time deciding whether a name may be added stays in that step
Manager time on duplicates the rule missed stays in the review

incremental.description: Revise required fields when a new event type is added to the register
Stores resubmit a row rejected for a missing store or date

approvals.approved_version: register rules signed for this period
name entry signed for this request

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes events still arrive as mail, so the alarm list is rarely complete and the manager still rekeys. The high case assumes clean alarm rows file themselves, while every name and every unclear duplicate stays with the manager. Identity matching is not treated as saved because it is not built.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Paperwork gaps and alarm lists become fields the manager reviews, procedure text is signed before stores see it, and a name reaches the offender report only when the manager writes it.
reach: Store managers receive the signed investigation procedure and the paperwork gaps to correct.
A compliance manager can read which register rules are signed and which names a person added.
skills_to_grow: Treat a missing count as a field error, not a verdict on a person.
Write a procedure that leaves interviews and named decisions with a person.
Keep a name off the offender report until a person types it.
role.ambitious_version: Every store works from one signed investigation procedure, and alarm activations are a list by device rather than a spreadsheet rebuilt each week.
